_note: What an operator wears, as clothing rather than as kit (src/game/outfit.ts). The kit in gear.json is the hard stuff strapped on top: plates, a helmet, a mask. This is the clothes under it, and it is what makes one figure a soldier and another a man in a t-shirt. Every piece is a shell along a bone, and every bone in this rig points along its own +y with a measured length (thigh 0.400 m, calf 0.429, upper arm 0.274, forearm 0.273), so a sleeve is a tube from 0 to a fraction of that length and nothing has to be rigged or weighted. Sizes are metres on a figure 1.8 m tall; colours are hex strings.

fit._note: the body's own thicknesses, which the clothes sit just outside of
fit._profile: how thick the body is along each bone: metres from the bone's own axis, six samples from the start of the bone to its end. Measured off the model by tools/checks/body.ts, which checks these numbers against it. A limb is not a cylinder, and a garment built on one number is either inside the body at the wide end (the arm is 84 mm at the shoulder) or a barrel at the narrow one (61 mm at the elbow).
fit._body: the body up the spine bone, band by band, the way the limbs are measured along theirs: six bands from `from` to `to` of the bone's length, each with the body's width, its depth and where its middle sits front to back. Measured off the model by tools/checks/body.ts. The spine bone leans back, so the middle drifts from +20 mm at the hips to -69 mm at the shoulders; one box on that axis is too wide at the waist, too shallow at the chest and 90 mm out at the collar, which is where the body used to stand out of its own jacket.
fit._gone: torso and torsoAt were one box and one offset for the whole body, typed in by eye. They are replaced by `body` above, measured band by band, and nothing reads them any more.
fit._torso: How the body under published cloth is narrowed so the cloth closes on it, per body, in metres up the bind pose. The garments are cut for the pack's Regular build and the free tier ships Superhero, so the chest is brought in towards `chest` between `from` and `to`, and eased back out to nothing between `neck` and `head` so the head keeps its own width and the hair and hood still fit it. Anything further than `armFrom` from the middle is an arm, out at shoulder height in the bind pose, and is left alone by `armTo`. Measured by width bands off each body (|x| < 0.19): the male's shoulders top out at y 1.50 (half-width 189 mm) and the neck is 105 mm at 1.55; the female's shoulders top out at 1.45 and the neck is 63 mm at 1.50. The female body wears the male garments and is already narrower than the body they were cut for, so it is not brought in at all. A build's `shoulders` multiplies both this and the garments over it by the same amount, so the fit between them holds. The ease-out starts above the shoulder line, not at it: starting at 1.48 on the male let the tops of the traps back out from under the coat and showed skin at the shoulder blades from behind. The male's neck is narrowest (70 mm) at 1.60, which is where the narrowing is gone. `upperArm` brings the upper arm in around its own bone, fully to 60% of the way to the elbow and back to nothing at it, so the forearm and hand do not move. Measured around upperarm_l, 95th-percentile radius in fifths from shoulder to elbow: the male body 101 / 102 / 104 / 90 / 73 mm, the Ranger sleeve 66 / 63 / 60 / 58 / 54, the Peasant sleeve 69 / 67 / 66 / 64 / 62. With the 22 mm shell the sleeve is still 15 to 20 mm short through the deltoid, which showed as skin at the back of every shoulder; 0.8 puts 104 at 83.
fit._undersuit: The colour the body's skin is taken to where the clothes always cover it, as a multiply over the skin texture. The garments are cut for a body the free tier does not ship, and every seam between two pieces - the armhole, the back of the knee, the ankle - was cut against a different outline, so after the body is shaped some skin still shows through at the seams. A dark undersuit makes a seam read as fabric or shadow instead. What stays skin is decided by the skin weights: the head, the neck, the forearms (the peasant sleeves stop short of the wrist) and the hands.
fit._overCloth: How far, in metres, the layer of a published garment against the skin is pushed out along its own normals. A garment sits exactly on the skin it was modelled over, so without it the two surfaces fight over the same pixels. tools/checks/body.ts checks the narrowed upper arm still fits inside every sleeve with it.

_builds: How heavy-set a figure is. The skeleton underneath, and so every hit box, is the same whatever the build: a game where a bigger-looking character is easier to hit is a game where nobody picks them. On published cloth `shoulders` is the width of the chest, body and garments together by the same amount, eased in up the torso and out again at the neck, so the fit between the cloth and the body holds at every build (src/game/mannequin.ts shapeTorso). The arms, the legs and the head keep their size. `cloth` is the thickness of the garments built in code, which only the fallback wears.
_bodies: The two bodies a player can pick, each the same 65-joint skeleton and so the same hit boxes. Every garment binds to either one, so the body is a choice of its own rather than something an outfit decides; an outfit's `body` is only what it wears when nobody has chosen. A body's `hair` swaps what an outfit names for what suits that body: an outfit's hair was chosen for the male body, so on the lighter one the beard goes and the short styles become the long one. null drops it.
_pieces: a piece with no kind is a shell along its bone, turned along the body's own profile. 'rags' hangs strips off one, which is what breaks a silhouette rather than colouring it; 'stripe' runs a band down the outside of one, which is what a tracksuit is.
_head: the things that cover a face, in the head bone's rest frame: x its right, y up it, z in front of it. A wrap is a shell round the skull with a tail down the back; goggles are two round lenses on a strap; a full mask covers the whole face, where the gas mask in gear.json covers the nose and mouth.

head._mxHelmet: a motocross helmet: a shell round the whole skull, a dark visor band where the eyes are, a chin bar across the jaw and a peak over the brow. It covers a face on its own, which is why the set that wears it needs nothing else on its own. Every number is against the head measured off the model by tools/checks/body.ts: 173 mm across, -9 to 256 mm up the Head bone, and a face that reaches 106 mm forward of it.
head._measured: Every number here is against the body the game now draws (public/models/body), measured by tools/checks/body.ts: the head is 159 mm across, runs 3 to 194 mm up the Head bone, reaches 124 mm forward, and its eyes are at y 69. The grey mannequin's head was 62 mm taller with its eyes 30 mm higher, which is where these numbers used to be and why a helmet floated above the head.

_sets: The outfits: what each wears, and in what colours. `cloth` is the main garment, `trim` the second colour, `boots` the footwear. An operator names one of these (src/game/operators.ts), and the kit in gear.json goes on top of it.
_realSets: A set with `character` is a real asset: a whole clothed figure, mesh and textures, from Quaternius's CC0 Modular Character Outfits (public/models/outfits, tools/fetch-characters.ts). The game swaps the figure's own mesh for it and builds no garments of its own, because its clothes ARE the mesh. Everything without `character` is built in code out of shells on bones, which is cheap, fits any rig and looks like what it is. A set's `hair` is one or two of the four rigged head meshes in public/models/body/hair, worn on the same skeleton as everything else and left in the pack's own colour: hair is not painted by the outfit's tint. A hood only clears a buzz cut, so anything with Ranger_Head_Hood gets that one; the long style is for the sets cut for the lighter body. The pack's hair textures are greyscale masks, mean 143 of 255 measured off the webp, because the pack expects the engine to colour them; `hairColor` is that colour, multiplied through the mask. Without it every figure has white hair. The wardrobe's variety comes out of mixing the two sets rather than recolouring one: a body from one and legs from the other, hood on or off, plate on the shoulder or not. Sixteen combinations of the male parts and four of the female, every one of them a different outline, which is what a player reads at eighty metres before any colour reaches them. The sets cut for the lighter body wear the MALE garments on it. The pack's female tops are corsets with bare shoulders and a low neckline, which is the asset rather than a fault, and it is not what an operator in a shooter wears: the male pieces are full coverage and bind to the same 65 joints, so they hang on either body. There were four more, RANGER (F), WORKWEAR (F), SCOUT (F) and HOODED (F), which were an outfit on the other body. The body is a choice of its own now (`bodies`), so those were the same clothes twice in the picker; a loadout that stored one gets the matching outfit on the lighter body (src/game/loadouts.ts).
